name: Dimethyltrienolone (Dimethyltren / RU-2420)

lead: Dimethyltrienolone (RU-2420) is an experimental oral anabolic steroid first described in 1967 by Roussel Uclaf and never sold as a medicine. It comes up in bodybuilding circles for its reported potency, aimed at more muscle mass.

It activates the androgen and progesterone receptors strongly and, like trenbolone, is not converted by aromatase or 5-alpha-reductase; methyl groups at two positions resist liver breakdown, allowing oral activity. Animal bioassays reported more than 100 times the potency of methyltestosterone, and Wikipedia attributes the description 'perhaps the most potent' to a secondary source. All of this rests on rodent and receptor-binding work.

paras: It circulates only as an unregulated research chemical taken orally; it has no approved form.
No human safety data exist. Reference sources describe it as expected to be highly liver-toxic, inferred from related compounds, and note progestogenic effects. It has no approved medical use.

angle.text: A never-marketed trenbolone analog that binds the androgen receptor very strongly in animal assays, which is why it comes up for muscle gain. No human studies exist, so its effect on physique is based on rodent and receptor work.

lead: Dimethyltrienolone (RU-2420, dimethyltren) is an experimental, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 7-alpha,17-alpha-dimethyl derivative of trenbolone. It was never marketed as a medicine. In bodybuilding and muscle-building forums it is mentioned as one of the most potent anabolic compounds ever synthesised, in the context of building muscle mass for a bigger, more muscular physique.[1][2]

Wikipedia reports that in animal bioassays it had more than 100 times the anabolic and androgenic potency of methyltestosterone, that it was first described in 1967 and that it was never marketed.[1] It binds the androgen and progesterone receptors strongly and is not converted by aromatase or 5-alpha-reductase.[1][2]

No human studies exist. Wikipedia describes the compound as expected to be exceedingly hepatotoxic, and forum members discussing it commonly treat it as a cautionary extreme rather than a practical option.[1][3][4]

paras: Dimethyltrienolone is an agonist of the androgen receptor that also activates the progesterone receptor, so it acts as both an anabolic steroid and a progestogen. Wikipedia lists relative binding affinities of about 180 percent at the androgen receptor and 306 percent at the progesterone receptor compared with testosterone, with negligible estrogen receptor binding of about 0.1 percent.[1]

Like trenbolone, it is not a substrate for 5-alpha-reductase or aromatase, so it is not converted into more potent androgens in tissues such as prostate or skin and has no estrogenic activity.[1][2] The 17-alpha-methyl group and the 7-alpha-methyl group are described as providing oral activity and resistance to metabolism, which are also said to make it exceedingly hepatotoxic.[1][2] Human pharmacokinetic data are unavailable.[2]

It is a derivative of trenbolone carrying methyl groups at the 7-alpha and 17-alpha positions, with the triene unsaturation of the trenbolone family. The reported formula is C20H26O2 with a molar mass of about 298.4 g/mol.[2]

The compound was developed under the RU code series of Roussel Uclaf, a French pharmaceutical company, and first described in 1967 during structure-activity work on nortestosterone derivatives. It was never developed as a drug.[1][2]

Dimethyltrienolone has no approved status in any jurisdiction and, where it appears, is sold as a research chemical.[2] Wikipedia notes that much of what is said about its potency comes from animal bioassays, receptor-binding studies and a popular book on steroids rather than clinical work.[1]

On T Nation it appears mostly in passing. One poster raised it as an example of a compound so toxic that it might carry acute-toxicity risk, another reply urged others to stay away from a related compound after a death reported on another site, and a 2018 thread asked whether anyone had tried methyltrienolone or dimethyltrienolone.[3][4][5] Comparison tables circulated in forum threads list its receptor binding relative to other steroids.[6]
No studies found. Only animal bioassays and receptor-binding experiments of the compound have been reported.[1][2]

lore.intro: On T Nation, dimethyltrienolone is mentioned as an extreme-potency reference point more than a compound members report using.[3][4][5]

claims.claim: It is among the most potent anabolic steroids ever made
